# Security Checklist: ISK-0002 — Public Contracts & Versioning Discipline

**Purpose**: Check that the security, tenant-isolation, and disclosure requirements for IDs, owner scopes, errors, and the request context are complete, clear, and consistent
**Created**: 2026-11-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Identifiers and Owner Scope

- [x] CHK001 - Is the entropy source and minimum entropy of a resource ID specified, along with the behavior when the source fails? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, FR-012]
- [x] CHK002 - Is it specified that an ID encodes no owner, time, sequence, or host, and is that measurable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006, SC-004]
  - T007 fixes the time representations SC-004 searches for (`yyyyMMdd`, and Unix seconds and milliseconds in decimal and base32). These are long enough that a random 26-character body will not contain them by chance across 1,000,000 IDs.
- [x] CHK003 - Is the canonical form defined tightly enough that each ID has exactly one text form? [Clarity, Contract §`resource-id` version 1, Research R6]
- [x] CHK004 - Is it specified that a parse failure echoes no more than a bounded, sanitized excerpt of the input? [Completeness, Spec §US2 scenario 3, Tasks T007]
- [x] CHK005 - Is it specified that the operator scope can never equal, convert into, or stand in for a tenant scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is the route for creating a trusted scoped reference (a protected `OwnershipResolver.Attest`, with harness rule H6 listing allowed subclasses) confirmed as the accepted design for FR-011? [Assumption, Spec §FR-011, Research R7, Contract rule H6]
  - **Needs a human decision.** The plan flagged R7 for reviewer confirmation, and no confirmation is recorded. Its limits: reflection can call `Attest`, and H6 scans only this repository's `src/` projects, so any assembly outside the repository can subclass `OwnershipResolver`. Such assemblies include in-process plugins, which `docs/11` treats as trusted, and an embedding application. The contract's known limits now say this.
- [x] CHK007 - Is a gateway correlation ID kept from being read as a resource ID, both by type and by text? [Consistency, Research R12, Contract §Resource types]
  - Fixed: `RequestCorrelationId` was a separate type, but nothing stopped a later spec from registering the prefix `req`, after which a correlation ID would parse as a resource ID. The contract, data model, and T006 now reserve `req`.
- [x] CHK008 - Is it specified that provider-native identifiers cannot be represented as resource IDs? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]

## Error Disclosure

- [x] CHK009 - Is the list of content that must never reach a client error explicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023]
- [x] CHK010 - Is the client-visible message protected by construction rather than by sanitizing free text? [Clarity, Research R9]
  - The message is always the code's registered safe message.
- [x] CHK011 - Are the requirements for a missing resource and another tenant's resource consistent across every envelope field, including `redaction_status`? [Consistency, Spec §TR-3, SC-006, FR-022]
  - Fixed: `redaction_status` was `withheld` whenever diagnostics were non-empty. If the foreign-tenant path attached diagnostics and the missing path did not, the field would tell the two apart, breaking SC-006. FR-022, the contract, the data model, and T013 and T014 now fix `redaction_status` at `withheld` for the `not_found` category.
- [x] CHK012 - Are bounds and character sets specified for every client-visible field that can carry provider-supplied or configured text? [Completeness, Contract §`error-envelope` version 1, Data model `ProviderErrorMetadata`]
  - Fixed: `provider.name` had a length bound but no character set, unlike `provider.error_code`. It now has the same character set (contract, data model, T012).
- [x] CHK013 - Is retry advice after visible streamed output forbidden for every category? [Completeness, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is the category given to the `docs/08` reason `auth_denied` (`identity.auth_denied` under `permission_denied`) confirmed as matching what `docs/08` means by it? [Ambiguity, Research R10, `docs/08` Operational controls]
  - **Needs a human decision.** The plan flagged R10 for reviewer confirmation, and no confirmation is recorded. `docs/08` lists `auth_denied` only as a reason code, without defining it. If it covers a failed authentication, its category is `unauthenticated`. If it covers a denied authorization, it is `permission_denied`, as planned. The module names given to the other four reasons (`policy`, `governance`, `routing`) come from the same research entry.

## Request Context Isolation

- [x] CHK015 - Is it specified that a context is request-local, with no static or ambient state, and that set-once values cannot change? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, FR-018, Research R8]
- [x] CHK016 - Is it specified what an extension-facing view must never expose, and is that checkable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-017, Contract rule H7]
- [x] CHK017 - Are caller-supplied correlation values bounded, restricted, and kept out of keys, log templates, and authorization? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, Contract §Request context]
- [x] CHK018 - Is the behavior for a deadline that has already passed when the context is created specified, and is it clear which spec stops the upstream call? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019, Edge Cases]
  - Fixed: the edge case said the request "does not proceed to an upstream call", which no requirement here covers. It now says that the specs that make upstream calls enforce this, and that this spec only reports expiry.

## Threat Model and Known Limits

- [x] CHK019 - Does every negative scenario in the spec trace to a requirement? [Traceability, Spec §Negative Security and Failure Scenarios]
- [x] CHK020 - Does the threat model say which attacks the harness defends against, and which it leaves to review? [Completeness, Contract §Threat model and known limits]
- [x] CHK021 - Is the gap between holding diagnostics apart and filtering them before logging recorded as a known limit, with its owning spec? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023, Contract §Known limits]
  - The maintainer decided this in analyze (D1). Filtering belongs to Telemetry/Audit (ISK-0071).
- [x] CHK022 - Is the fact that review of protected files is requested, not enforced, stated with its exception? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Contract header]
  - DEC-20261105-002. `/src/Iskender.Core.Contracts/` is already in `.github/CODEOWNERS`, so the registry sources are covered.
